1.o: This chapter is a general preface to the whole book, and contains, I. An inscription, declaring the original and the design of it, ver. 1, 2. II. The apostolic benediction pronounced on all those who shall pay a due regard to the contents of this book, ver. 3-8. III. A glorious vision or appearance of the Lord Jesus Christ to the apostle John, when he delivered to him this revelation, ver. 9, to the end.
1.i: John, exiled on Patmos, sees the risen Jesus walking among seven golden lampstands.
1.p: Lord Jesus, You walk among Your people. We worship You, the First and the Last. Amen.
1.l: Say hello to Jesus out loud today, and tell Him you are glad He is alive.
q: Jesus' first words to John were do not be afraid. What do you need to hear Him say?

2.o: The apostle John, having in the foregoing chapter written the things which he had seen, now proceeds to write the things that are, according to the command of God (ch. i. 19), that is, the present state of the seven churches of Asia, with which he had a particular acquaintance, and for which he had a tender concern.
2.s: You Have Abandoned Your First Love
2.i: Jesus praises the church at Ephesus for hard work and truth but warns that they have lost their first love.
2.p: Lord Jesus, rekindle our first love for You. Help us not to do good things without a loving heart. Amen.
2.l: Do something today just because you love Jesus, not because you have to.
q: The Ephesians did good things but lost their first love. How can you keep love at the center?

3.o: Here we have three more of the epistles of Christ to the churches: I. To Sardis, ver. 1-6. II. To Philadelphia, ver. 7-13. III. To Laodicea, ver. 14, to the end.
3.i: Jesus tells the church in Sardis, which looks alive but is dying, to wake up and remember.
3.p: Lord, wake us up. Strengthen what is weak in us and keep us watchful for You. Amen.
3.l: Do something today you have been putting off for God, and don't wait until later.
q: Sardis had a good name but was spiritually asleep. What would wake you up?

4.o: In this chapter the prophetical scene opens; and, as the epistolary part opened with a vision of Christ (ch. i.), so this part is introduced with a glorious appearance of the great God, whose throne is in heaven, compassed about with the heavenly host. This discovery was made to John, and in this chapter he, I. Records the heavenly sight he saw, ver. 1-7. And then, II. The heavenly songs he heard, ver. 8, to the end.
4.i: Revelation 4 and 5 open the door to heaven: a throne, a scroll nobody could open, and a Lamb who could.
4.p: Lord God Almighty, we worship You. Lamb who was slain, we praise You, for You are worthy. Amen.
4.l: Sing or say a praise today, and picture a huge crowd of every nation singing it with you.
q: John looked for a lion and saw a lamb. How does that change what strength looks like?

5.o: In the foregoing chapter the prophetical scene was opened, in the sight and hearing of the apostle, and he had a sight of God the Creator and ruler of the world, and the great King of the church. He saw God on the throne of glory and government, surrounded with his holy ones, and receiving their adorations. Now the counsels and decrees of God are set before the apostle, as in a book, which God held in his right hand; and this book is represented, I. As sealed in the hand of God, ver. 1-9. II.
5.i: Revelation 4 and 5 open the door to heaven: a throne, a scroll nobody could open, and a Lamb who could.
5.p: Lord God Almighty, we worship You. Lamb who was slain, we praise You, for You are worthy. Amen.
5.l: Sing or say a praise today, and picture a huge crowd of every nation singing it with you.
q: John looked for a lion and saw a lamb. How does that change what strength looks like?

6.o: The book of the divine counsels being thus lodged in the hand of Christ, he loses no time, but immediately enters upon the work of opening the seals and publishing the contents; but this is done in such a manner as still leaves the predictions very abstruse and difficult to be understood. Hitherto the waters of the sanctuary have been as those in Ezekiel's vision, only to the ankles, or to the knees, or to the loins at least; but here they begin to be a river that cannot be passed over.
6.s: The Seals and the Great Crowd
6.i: Revelation 6 and 7 contain some of the hardest and some of the most comforting scenes in the book.
6.p: Lamb of God, be our shepherd. Wipe away every tear, and bring us home. Amen.
6.l: Today say hello to someone in a language that is not your own, even if it is only one word.
q: Revelation has frightening scenes and comforting ones. Which do you tend to remember?

7.o: The things contained in this chapter came in after the opening of the six seals, which foretold great calamities in the world; and before the sound of the seven trumpets, which gave notice of great corruptions arising in the church: between these comes in this comfortable chapter, which secures the graces and comforts of the people of God in times of common calamity. We have, I. An account of the restraint laid upon the winds, ver. 1-3. II. The sealing of the servants of God, ver. 4-8. III.
7.s: The Seals and the Great Crowd
7.i: Revelation 6 and 7 contain some of the hardest and some of the most comforting scenes in the book.
7.p: Lamb of God, be our shepherd. Wipe away every tear, and bring us home. Amen.
7.l: Today say hello to someone in a language that is not your own, even if it is only one word.
q: Revelation has frightening scenes and comforting ones. Which do you tend to remember?

8.o: We have already seen what occurred upon opening six of the seals; we now come to the opening of the seventh, which introduced the sounding of the seven trumpets; and a direful scene now opens. Most expositors agree that the seven seals represent the interval between the apostle's time and the reign of Constantine, but that the seven trumpets are designed to represent the rise of antichrist, some time after the empire became Christian. In this chapter we have, I.
8.i: Revelation 8 to 11 mix trumpets, a little scroll and two witnesses, and end with the kingdom of the world becoming the kingdom of Christ.
8.p: Lord, You reign forever and ever. Hold us steady while we wait, and keep our prayers rising like incense. Amen.
8.l: Sit in silence for a few minutes today, say nothing, and listen, as heaven did.
q: There are several guesses about who the two witnesses are. How do you like to read puzzles in the Bible?

9.o: In this chapter we have an account of the sounding of the fifth and sixth trumpets, the appearances that attended them, and the events that were to follow; the fifth trumpet (ver. 1-12), the sixth, ver. 13, &c..
9.i: Revelation 8 to 11 mix trumpets, a little scroll and two witnesses, and end with the kingdom of the world becoming the kingdom of Christ.
9.p: Lord, You reign forever and ever. Hold us steady while we wait, and keep our prayers rising like incense. Amen.
9.l: Sit in silence for a few minutes today, say nothing, and listen, as heaven did.
q: There are several guesses about who the two witnesses are. How do you like to read puzzles in the Bible?

10.o: This chapter is an introduction to the latter part of the prophecies of this book. Whether what is contained between this and the sounding of the seventh trumpet (ch. xi. 15) be a distinct prophecy from the other, or only a more general account of some of the principal things included in the other, is disputed by our curious enquirers into these abstruse writings. However, here we have, I. A remarkable description of a very glorious angel with an open book in his hand, ver. 1-3. II.
10.i: Revelation 8 to 11 mix trumpets, a little scroll and two witnesses, and end with the kingdom of the world becoming the kingdom of Christ.
10.p: Lord, You reign forever and ever. Hold us steady while we wait, and keep our prayers rising like incense. Amen.
10.l: Sit in silence for a few minutes today, say nothing, and listen, as heaven did.
q: There are several guesses about who the two witnesses are. How do you like to read puzzles in the Bible?

11.o: In this chapter we have an account, I. Of the measuring—reed given to the apostle, to take the dimensions of the temple, ver. 1, 2. II. Of the two witnesses of God, ver. 3-13. III. Of the sounding of the seventh trumpet, and what followed upon it, ver. 14, &c.
11.i: Revelation 8 to 11 mix trumpets, a little scroll and two witnesses, and end with the kingdom of the world becoming the kingdom of Christ.
11.p: Lord, You reign forever and ever. Hold us steady while we wait, and keep our prayers rising like incense. Amen.
11.l: Sit in silence for a few minutes today, say nothing, and listen, as heaven did.
q: There are several guesses about who the two witnesses are. How do you like to read puzzles in the Bible?

12.o: It is generally agreed by the most learned expositors that the narrative we have in this and the two following chapters, from the sounding of the seventh trumpet to the opening of the vials, is not a prediction of things to come, but rather a recapitulation and representation of things past, which, as God would have the apostle to foresee while future, he would have him to review now that they were past, that he might have a more perfect idea of them in his mind, and might observe the agreement between the…
12.s: The Woman, the Dragon and the Lamb
12.i: Revelation 12 to 14 are a picture-story of a woman, a dragon, and a Lamb who wins.
12.p: Lord, thank You for the safe places You prepare. Help us trust You through the war and the waiting. Amen.
12.l: Say thank you out loud for a place where you feel safe, and think of someone who has none.
q: The woman flees to a place God has prepared. When have you found a place that was ready before you needed it?

13.o: We have, in this chapter, a further discovery and description of the church's enemies: not other enemies than are mentioned before, but described after another manner, that the methods of their enmity may more fully appear. They are represented as two beasts; the first you have an account of (ver. 1-10) the second, ver. 11, &c.
13.s: The Woman, the Dragon and the Lamb
13.i: Revelation 12 to 14 are a picture-story of a woman, a dragon, and a Lamb who wins.
13.p: Lord, thank You for the safe places You prepare. Help us trust You through the war and the waiting. Amen.
13.l: Say thank you out loud for a place where you feel safe, and think of someone who has none.
q: The woman flees to a place God has prepared. When have you found a place that was ready before you needed it?

14.o: After an account of the great trials and sufferings which the servants of God had endured, we have now a more pleasant scene opening; the day begins now to dawn, and here we have represented, I. The Lord Jesus at the head of his faithful followers, ver. 1-5. II. Three angels sent successively to proclaim the fall of Babylon and the things antecedent and consequent to so great an event, ver. 6-13. III. The vision of the harvest, ver. 14, &c.
14.s: The Woman, the Dragon and the Lamb
14.i: Revelation 12 to 14 are a picture-story of a woman, a dragon, and a Lamb who wins.
14.p: Lord, thank You for the safe places You prepare. Help us trust You through the war and the waiting. Amen.
14.l: Say thank you out loud for a place where you feel safe, and think of someone who has none.
q: The woman flees to a place God has prepared. When have you found a place that was ready before you needed it?

15.o: Hitherto, according to the judgment of very eminent expositors, God had represented to his servant, John, I. The state of the church under the pagan powers, in the six seals opened; and then, II. The state of the church under the papal powers, in the vision of the six trumpets that began to sound upon the opening of the seventh seal: and then is inserted. III. A more general and brief account of the past, present, and future state of the church, in the little book, &c. He now proceeds, IV.
15.s: The Bowls and the Fall of Babylon
15.i: Revelation 15 to 18 pour out the last bowls and show the fall of Babylon, a symbol of pride and wealth.
15.p: Lord, You are just and true. Keep us from loving what falls, and help us come out of whatever takes us from You. Amen.
15.l: Notice one thing today that looks beautiful but takes more than it gives, such as a sale, a trend or a screen.
q: Babylon is a picture, not just a place. What would you say Babylon stands for today?

16.o: In this chapter we have an account of the pouring forth of these vials that were filled with the wrath of God. They were poured out upon the whole antichristian empire, and on every thing appertaining to it. I. Upon the earth, ver. 2. II. Upon the sea, ver. 3. III. Upon the rivers and fountains of water, ver. 4. Here the heavenly hosts proclaim and applaud the righteousness of the judgments of God. IV. The fourth vial was poured out on the sun, ver. 8. V. The fifth on the seat of the beast. VI.
16.s: The Bowls and the Fall of Babylon
16.i: Revelation 15 to 18 pour out the last bowls and show the fall of Babylon, a symbol of pride and wealth.
16.p: Lord, You are just and true. Keep us from loving what falls, and help us come out of whatever takes us from You. Amen.
16.l: Notice one thing today that looks beautiful but takes more than it gives, such as a sale, a trend or a screen.
q: Babylon is a picture, not just a place. What would you say Babylon stands for today?

17.o: This chapter contains another representation of those things that had been revealed before concerning the wickedness and ruin of antichrist. This antichrist had been before represented as a beast, and is now described as a great whore. And here, I. The apostle is invited to see this vile woman, ver. 1, 2. II. He tells us what an appearance she made, ver. 3-6. III. The mystery of it is explained to him, ver. 7-12. And, IV. Her ruin foretold, ver. 13, &c.
17.s: The Bowls and the Fall of Babylon
17.i: Revelation 15 to 18 pour out the last bowls and show the fall of Babylon, a symbol of pride and wealth.
17.p: Lord, You are just and true. Keep us from loving what falls, and help us come out of whatever takes us from You. Amen.
17.l: Notice one thing today that looks beautiful but takes more than it gives, such as a sale, a trend or a screen.
q: Babylon is a picture, not just a place. What would you say Babylon stands for today?

18.o: We have here, I. An angel proclaiming the fall of Babylon, ver. 1, 2. II. Assigning the reasons of her fall, ver. 3. III. Giving warning to all who belonged to God to come out of her (ver. 4, 5), and to assist in her destruction, ver. 6-8. IV. The great lamentation made for her by those who had been large sharers in her sinful pleasures and profits, ver. 9-19. V. The great joy that there would be among others at the sight of her irrecoverable ruin, ver. 20, &c.
18.s: The Bowls and the Fall of Babylon
18.i: Revelation 15 to 18 pour out the last bowls and show the fall of Babylon, a symbol of pride and wealth.
18.p: Lord, You are just and true. Keep us from loving what falls, and help us come out of whatever takes us from You. Amen.
18.l: Notice one thing today that looks beautiful but takes more than it gives, such as a sale, a trend or a screen.
q: Babylon is a picture, not just a place. What would you say Babylon stands for today?

19.o: In this chapter we have, I. A further account of the triumphant song of angels and saints for the fall of Babylon, ver. 1-4. II. The marriage between Christ and the church proclaimed and perfected, ver. 5-10. III. Another warlike expedition of the glorious head and husband of the church, with the success of it, ver. 10, &c.
19.s: The Rider on the White Horse
19.i: Revelation 19 and 20 celebrate a wedding, show a rider on a white horse, and end with the final judgment.
19.p: King of kings and Lord of lords, we praise You. Prepare us for the wedding supper of the Lamb. Amen.
19.l: Write one thing you can do today that is a good deed, and do it as though it were part of a robe.
q: No one can break Christ's seal. What is shut in your life that you keep trying to pry open?

20.o: This chapter is thought by some to be the darkest part of all this prophecy: it is very probable that the things contained in it are not yet accomplished; and therefore it is the wiser way to content ourselves with general observations, rather than to be positive and particular in our explications of it. Here we have an account, I. Of the binding of Satan for a thousand years, ver. 1-3. II. The reign of the saints with Christ for the same time, ver. 4-6. III.
20.s: The Rider on the White Horse
20.i: Revelation 19 and 20 celebrate a wedding, show a rider on a white horse, and end with the final judgment.
20.p: King of kings and Lord of lords, we praise You. Prepare us for the wedding supper of the Lamb. Amen.
20.l: Write one thing you can do today that is a good deed, and do it as though it were part of a robe.
q: No one can break Christ's seal. What is shut in your life that you keep trying to pry open?

21.o: Hitherto the prophecy of this book has presented to us a very remarkable mixture of light and shade, prosperity and adversity, mercy and judgment, in the conduct of divine Providence towards the church in the world: now, at the close of all, the day breaks, and the shadows flee away; a new world now appears, the former having passed away.
21.i: Revelation 21 and 22 end the Bible with a new world, a city with open gates, and a river, a tree, and a promise.
21.p: Come, Lord Jesus. Make all things new, and wipe away every tear. Amen.
21.l: Plant a seed or water a plant today, and think of the tree of life, whose leaves are for healing.
q: A gate stood for the whole city. What is the 'gate' of your home, the place where decisions and welcomes happen?

22.o: In this chapter we have, I. A further description of the heavenly state of the church, ver. 1-5. II. A confirmation of this and all the other visions of this book, ver. 6-19. III. The conclusion, ver. 20, 21.
22.i: Revelation 21 and 22 end the Bible with a new world, a city with open gates, and a river, a tree, and a promise.
22.p: Come, Lord Jesus. Make all things new, and wipe away every tear. Amen.
22.l: Plant a seed or water a plant today, and think of the tree of life, whose leaves are for healing.
q: A gate stood for the whole city. What is the 'gate' of your home, the place where decisions and welcomes happen?
